misconceptions.name: Aromaticity by ring alone
misconceptions.description: Calls any cyclic conjugated ring aromatic without applying all four criteria.

misconceptions.name: Benzene undergoes addition
misconceptions.description: Applies alkene addition chemistry to an aromatic ring.

misconceptions.name: Directing effects from electronegativity alone
misconceptions.description: Predicts orientation from induction and ignores resonance donation.

misconceptions.name: Friedel Crafts on any ring
misconceptions.description: Attempts alkylation on strongly deactivated rings or with rearranging substrates.

misconceptions.name: Epoxide opening regiochemistry ignored
misconceptions.description: Uses the same attack position under acidic and basic conditions.

misconceptions.name: Carbonyl reactivity ladder inverted
misconceptions.description: Attempts to make an acid chloride from an amide directly.

misconceptions.name: Grignard with acidic protons present
misconceptions.description: Uses an organometallic reagent alongside an alcohol, acid or amine.

misconceptions.name: Ester Grignard stops at the ketone
misconceptions.description: Forgets the second addition that gives a tertiary alcohol.

misconceptions.name: Wrong alpha carbon enolized
misconceptions.description: Deprotonates a non alpha position, or ignores thermodynamic and kinetic control.

misconceptions.name: Aldol without dehydration
misconceptions.description: Stops at the beta hydroxy carbonyl when conditions force condensation.

misconceptions.name: Claisen run with catalytic base
misconceptions.description: Uses substoichiometric base, so the driving deprotonation never happens.

misconceptions.name: Amine basicity by substitution count only
misconceptions.description: Ignores resonance delocalization in anilines and amides.

misconceptions.name: Retrosynthesis run forwards
misconceptions.description: Proposes reagents instead of disconnections, so the analysis never simplifies.

misconceptions.name: Protecting groups omitted
misconceptions.description: Designs a route in which a reagent destroys a functional group elsewhere.

misconceptions.name: Anomers called enantiomers
misconceptions.description: Misclassifies alpha and beta anomers, which are diastereomers.
